frontmatter.title: How to Save Files with Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java

blocks.content: You will load `a` presentation file and save it in `a` different format using the `Presentation` class and its save() method. Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java supports saving to formats such as PPTX, PDF, and image formats via format-specific overloads of save().
You will load `a` presentation file and save it in another format using Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java. This requires Java 8 or later and the Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java library installed.

items: Java Development Kit (JDK) version 8 or higher
A valid `.pptx` file to load and process

blocks.content: You will load `a` presentation and save it to disk in the original `.pptx` format using the `Presentation` class and its save() method. Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java supports saving presentations with full fidelity to `.pptx` files.

items: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java JAR in your classpath

blocks.content: Load and Save `a` `Presentation`
Step 1: Load an existing presentation file using the `Presentation` constructor. Pass the path to the `.pptx` file as `a` string argument.

import com.aspose.slides.*;

Presentation presentation = new Presentation("input.pptx");
This creates `a` `Presentation` object representing the loaded file.
Save to `a` New Path
Step 2: Call save() on the `Presentation` object to write the file to `a` new location. Provide the output file path and format.
presentation.save("output.pptx", SaveFormat.Pptx);
This writes the modified presentation to `output.pptx` in the same `.pptx` format.
Save with Custom Options
Step 3: Use SaveOptions subclasses to control export behavior. For example, set compression or thumbnail size when saving to image formats.
This saves the presentation with maximum compression applied.
Error Handling
Wrap file operations in `try-catch` blocks to handle IOException or Exception thrown during load or save. Check for null inputs and valid file paths before calling save().
This ensures robust handling of missing or corrupted input files.
Next Steps
After saving, explore how to modify slide content, apply formatting, or export to other formats like PDF or images using the same save() method with appropriate `SaveFormat` values.

You will load an existing PowerPoint presentation, modify `a` slide's text content, and save the updated file using Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java. This example uses only the canonical import path and demonstrates core file I/O and text manipulation with verified API classes.

items: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java JAR in your classpath

blocks.content: Step 1: Load the presentation file. Use the `Presentation` class to open an existing `.pptx` file. This creates an in-memory representation of the entire presentation.

import com.aspose.slides.*;

Presentation pres = new Presentation("input.pptx");

Step 2: Access the first slide and modify its text. Retrieve the first slide, then locate `a` text frame or shape containing text. Update the portion text using `BasePortionFormat` and related classes.
Step 3: Save the modified presentation. Call save() on the `Presentation` object to write the updated content back to disk in `.pptx` format.
pres.save("output.pptx", SaveFormat.Pptx);

The code loads `input.pptx`, updates the first text portion on the first shape of the first slide, and saves the result as `output.pptx`. This demonstrates the minimal workflow for reading, modifying, and writing presentations using Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java.
